Definition: to push off; used in a great variety of applications, literally and figuratively (to expel, mislead, strike, inflict, etc.)
BiblicalUsage: Nadach means to be driven away or pushed off, and it is the word for exile and for straying sheep. In Deuteronomy 30:1 the Lord says the people will call the blessing and the curse to mind among all the nations where He has driven them, and in Jeremiah 23:2 the pastors have scattered the flock and driven them away. In Ezekiel 34:4 the shepherds have not brought again that which was driven away, and in Deuteronomy 30:4 even if the driven ones are at the outmost parts of heaven, the Lord will gather them from there.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe being driven away is the Bible's picture of what sin does to a people, but Deuteronomy 30:1 holds the way back in the same breath. The driven ones are told to call it all to mind, and remembering is the first step home. I hold that no exile is too far for the God who drove them to bring them back.
